# Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka (Ja 454)
**ID:** Ja 454
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja454
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Epigraphic and art-historical evidence from Pagan confirms that the story was well known in Burmese temple tradition under name variants such as *Ghatapandita*, *Satapandita*, and *Ghattamandita* [Win Than Tun 2002].
Scholars of comparative folklore have also compared narrative motifs found in the Jātaka to Western myths, such as the Greek story of Danae [Wick and Rabens 2013].
SuttaCentral notes verse and thematic parallels between Ja 454 and several other grief-consolation tales: *Sujātajātaka* (Ja 352), *Migapotakajātaka* (Ja 372), *Somadattajātaka* (Ja 410), and *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka* (Ja 449), alongside related narratives in the *Petavatthu* (Pv 8, Pv 17, Pv 18, Pv 25) and *Vimānavatthu* (Vv 83) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus corroborates these textual relationships through extensive verse sharing: Ja 454 §1.1–10.4 is nearly identical to *Kaṇhapetavatthu* (Pv 18), while the consolation verses in §11.4–15.4 recur verbatim or nearly verbatim across Ja 352, Ja 372, Ja 410, Ja 449, Pv 8, Pv 17, Pv 25, and Vv 83, as well as their commentaries in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels (SuttaCentral): Ja 352 Sujātajātaka; Ja 372 Migapotakajātaka; Ja 410 Somadattajātaka; Ja 449 Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka
- Mentioned in (SuttaCentral): Pv 8 Goṇapetavatthu; Pv 18 Kaṇhapetavatthu; Pv 17 Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu; Pv 25 Ubbaripetavatthu; Vv 83 Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0507a) (§11.4–15.4 ↔ §948–960); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Catuttho bhāgo) (Atk S0513a4) (§5.1–6.4 ↔ §758_1–762); Kaṇhapetavatthu (Pv 18) (§1.1–10.4 ↔ §0.3–10.4); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§12.1–15.3 ↔ §1320–1330); Sujātajātaka (Ja 352) (§11.4–15.3 ↔ §4.4–8.3); Goṇapetavatthu (Pv 8) (§11.4–15.3 ↔ §4.4–8.3); Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu (Vv 83) (§11.4–14.4 ↔ §7.4–10.4); Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu (Pv 17) (§12.1–14.4 ↔ §8.1–10.4)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): 鸚鵡經 (ZH_T01_0079) [zh]

- [Win Than Tun 2002] Win Than Tun, Buddhism Pagan period (2002) — Attests to the text and name variants in Pagan temple inscriptions.
